segments.text: Why was the first tunnel not completed?
segments.translation: 为什么第一条隧道没有完工？

segments.text: In 1858, a French engineer, Aime Thome de Gamond,
segments.translation: 1858年，一位名叫埃梅·托梅·德·加蒙的法国工程师

segments.text: arrived in England with a plan for a 21-mile tunnel under the English Channel.
segments.translation: 带着一份在英吉利海峡下开凿一条21英里长隧道的计划来到英国。

segments.text: He said that it would be possible to build a platform in the centre of the Channel.
segments.translation: 他说可以在海峡中央建造一个平台。

segments.text: This platform would serve as a port and a railway station.
segments.translation: 这个平台将用作港口和火车站。

segments.text: The tunnel would be well-ventilated if tall chimneys were built above sea level.
segments.translation: 如果在海面上建造高大的烟囱，隧道就会通风良好。

segments.text: In 1860, a better plan was put forward by an Englishman, William Low.
segments.translation: 1860年，一位名叫威廉·洛的英国人提出了一个更好的计划。

segments.text: He suggested that a double railway-tunnel should be built.
segments.translation: 他建议建造一条双轨铁路隧道。

segments.text: This would solve the problem of ventilation for if a train entered this tunnel, it would draw in fresh air behind it.
segments.translation: 这样就解决了通风问题，因为如果一列火车进入隧道，它就把新鲜空气带进去了。

segments.text: Forty-two years later a tunnel was actually begun.
segments.translation: 42年后，隧道实际上开始挖掘了。

segments.text: If, at the time, the British had not feared invasion, it would have been completed.
segments.translation: 如果当时英国人不是担心遭到入侵，隧道就完工了。

segments.text: The world had to wait almost another 100 years for the Channel Tunnel.
segments.translation: 世界不得不再等待差不多100年才看到英吉利海峡隧道。

segments.text: It was officially opened on March 7, 1994, finally connecting Britain to the European continent.
segments.translation: 它于1994年3月7日正式开通，终于把英国与欧洲大陆连接起来了。
